_status: ONE-SHOT ADMIN ENTRYPOINT for the owner-gated HALT reset. It is NOT a service: nothing runs it continuously, and it exists only to be pointed at the l5-halt-watchdog service for the duration of one reset and then pointed away. The halt latch is a file on that service's volume and a Railway volume mounts to exactly one service, so the reset must run there; this manifest is what keeps that temporary swap explicit rather than improvised. Auto-redeploy is disabled by a watch pattern that matches nothing -- deploying this is an owner action, exactly as for pmus_ws_book_diag. restartPolicyType NEVER because the script EXITS by design; ALWAYS would loop it and leave the watchdog not sweeping for longer. The image holds signing and a GET-only transport (pmus_auth.ReadOnlyTransport) and no order-placing code, so it cannot place or cancel anything at the venue; its only write is the halt object, and only after four fail-closed gates. L5_HALT_RESET_INSPECT=YES is the image default, so a bare boot performs the READ-ONLY dry run and writes nothing. Credentials are TEMPORARY and are removed immediately after; the credential-free watchdog image is never modified (OWNER 2026-10-14, preserved).
